# `maximum-increased`

maximum increased

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` in requests, `warn` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `maximum-increased` (both directions), `maximum-increased-in-request`, `maximum-increased-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

`maximum` or `exclusiveMaximum` increased.

## Why this default

In requests: more numbers are valid. In responses: clients may store values in types sized for the old maximum.

## Example

From test case [`maximum-increased`](../../test/cases/maximum-increased/): maximum raised on a response number.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: integer
-           maximum: 50
+           maximum: 100
```

Findings:

- `maximum-increased-in-response` · warn · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  maximum-increased: warn
```

## How to fix

Check that clients handle the larger values.
